- **Anthracnose**: Reference shows dark lesions on pods. Acervuli have visible spines (setae) -- "pin cushion" appearance. The test image dots don't show this morphology.
- **Diaporthe**: Black pycnidia on the *external surface* of mature stems, often in linear rows. The Diaporthe reference (bottom-right) shows a very similar pattern of black specks on a gray/bleached stem surface.

The test image shows black raised specks on the external surface of a dry, mature, grayish stem -- consistent with Diaporthe pycnidia. The specks show some linear arrangement along the stem axis. This matches the Diaporthe description of "Black, raised specks (pycnidia) appearing in linear rows on mature soybean stems."
